claims.text: A chemically disordered, single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti high-entropy alloy can serve as the initial material state.
The initial Fe-Co-Ni-Ti alloy has low coercivity because its orbital moments are suppressed.
Controlled annealing or rapid-solidification processing can create nanoscale Ti-rich intermetallic precipitates while retaining an fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti matrix.
The Ti-rich precipitates can adopt B2-ordered or L12-structured forms such as TiFe- or TiNi-related intermetallics.
Nanoscale precipitate–matrix interfaces act as magnetic domain-wall pinning sites.
The Ti-rich precipitates generate local lattice-strain fields in the fcc matrix.
Precipitate-induced strain modifies the electronic band structure and enhances orbital magnetic moments.
Exchange coupling between the fcc matrix and ordered precipitates counteracts orbital-moment suppression and alters the magnetic ground state.
Domain-wall pinning raises the energy barrier for magnetization reversal and therefore increases coercivity.
The proposed dual-phase alloy will exhibit coercivity above 100 Oe at temperatures above room temperature.
The dual-phase alloy will show a distinct hysteresis-loop shape attributable to separate magnetic contributions from the matrix and precipitates.
The alloy can retain matrix ductility and its primary fcc structure after precipitation.
A corresponding single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni-Ti control will have coercivity below 100 Oe because it lacks pinning sites and has suppressed orbital moments.
The beneficial effect requires precipitates smaller than 50 nm and a noncontinuous secondary-phase morphology.
Large or continuous Ti-rich intermetallic phases would degrade mechanical properties and disrupt fcc-matrix continuity.
Exceeding the Ti solubility limit will cause bulk phase separation.
Annealing time can be selected to produce nanoscale precipitates without progressing to bulk decomposition.
Rapid quenching can suppress precipitation sufficiently to create a single-phase control specimen.

contradictions.description: Rapid-solidification processing is proposed as a way to induce Ti-rich precipitation, whereas rapid quenching is also proposed as the means of suppressing precipitation to make the single-phase control. The processing distinction needed to reconcile these opposite roles is not specified.
